overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email among a quorum, and was ordered to release the emails. Other allegations were not violations or were declined as untimely or outside review.

allegations.summary: Board listed a Town Administrator job description and Collins Center report topic on nine meetings (Apr 18 to Jun 10) but did not discuss it. Review of Apr 18 to May 20 meetings declined.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deciding not to discuss the topics at its June 3 and June 10 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint covered seven meetings from April 18 to May 20 where a noticed topic was not discussed; filed too late, so review was declined.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complaint at issue here was filed with the Board on June 23, we limit our review to the Board meetings held on June 3 and June 10 and decline to review any allegations raised in the complaint for meetings held between April 18 and May 20.

allegations.summary: Board placed Article 19 on the Town Warrant without any open session discussion; allegation was generalized and whether the warrant placement was proper under other law was outside review.
allegations.key_passage: Thus we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Board could be a violation of some other law, including Town bylaws

allegations.summary: Minutes of Mar 18 to Apr 22 meetings allegedly insufficiently detailed or inaccurate; complaint was untimely because minutes were approved more than 30 days before filing.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint here was filed on June 23, more than 30 days after the date that the Board approved these five sets of minutes, and we therefore find these allegations to be untimely and decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Minutes of May 13, May 20, June 3 and June 10 allegedly lacked detail on Town Administrator and Collins Center discussions and omitted a list of documents used.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the minutes are accurate and sufficiently detailed, and the Board therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A quorum of Board members emailed each other about the Town Administrator position and Collins Center report between January and February, outside any posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating among a quorum via email and order the Board to publicly release these emails within 30 days of receipt of this determination, if it has not already done so.

allegations.summary: Request for further review alleged deliberation on a closed Google Group and in scheduling emails; these claims were not in the original complaint to the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these allegations were not raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review their merits.

remedy: Publicly release the emails within 30 days of receipt of the determination, to the extent not already released.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
